title: The dips of 118 TESS complex periodic variables stay at a fixed phase relative to the starspot pattern for months, then drift away as a random walk of 1e-5 cycles squared per day
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period, probably from material near corotation. We tested how the dip pattern moves relative to the starspot pattern of the same star. We split each folded TESS 2-minute light curve into a spot part (harmonics 1-2 with dip masks) and a dip part, and measured the phase of each part in 1.5-day chunks. We used 443 light curves (sectors 1-107) of 126 on-target CPVs from an earlier survey, and 3,300 injections into 300 non-CPV rapid rotators. Inside sectors, the dip phase scatters 4.1 (3.4-4.4) times less than the spot phase; CPV spots scatter like control spots. The mean fractional dip-minus-spot frequency is (-0.8 +/- 0.6)e-5 in 118 stars, so on average the material corotates to 2e-5 (95%). But the differences scatter 2.3 times more than calibrated errors, and the dip-minus-spot phase follows a random walk with D = 1.06 (0.86-1.31)e-5 cycles^2/day; strictly periodic injected dips give 0.04e-5. Between sectors, the fraction of pairs where the dips keep their phase relative to the spots within 0.05 cycles is 0.74 for gaps below 60 days, 0.36 for 60-400 days, 0.17 for 1-3 years and 0.14 for 3-8 years, against an injection null of 0.12. A random walk fitted to these pairs gives D = 1.0 (0.3-1.5)e-5, the same as inside sectors; the memory time is 166 (85-473) days. Deepest dips avoid the spot maximum (12% against 21%, p = 0.008), and dip pairs half a cycle apart are not common. Thus the stellar surface pattern sets the dip longitude for months, longer than single dips live, and the longitude then wanders as a random walk of about 0.06 cycles per year. Limitations: the spot/dip split is a model choice; template shifts mix motion and shape change; labels come from one automated vetter; no spectra. Code, per-unit TESS-derived measurements, injections, figures and hashes are included; TESS FITS files and Gaia records are not.

Middle: fraction of sector pairs with the dip pattern within 0.05 cycles of its earlier phase relative to the spots, with star-bootstrap 95% intervals and the injection null. Right: phase of the deepest dip relative to the spot minimum for 124 CPVs and for injected dips at random phases.
